attributes.axis_log: The pre-kit cap's residual label ('missing dead extsb/extsb/cmpw and dependent coloring') is CORRECT and its scale was understated: after the displacement arithmetic, those 3 instructions are the ENTIRE residual. Target @b8-cc: lbz r3,227(r7) / lbz r0,226(r30) / extsb r3,r3 / extsb r0,r0 / cmpw r3,r0 / addi r5,r5,1 -- a fully dead compare, since the next cr0 writer is the loop-latch cmpw. Ours emitted the two lbz (the volatile scaffold) but neither extsb nor the cmpw. Three forms probed (see probed_form). Form B is strictly better than the committed baseline on every instrument that moved and equal on the rest, and it retires a misleading source shape: the old `if (a != b) { continue; }` claimed a control transfer at a point where `continue` is the loop's own fallthrough, so the branch was always dead; the retained form states plainly that the comparison's result is unused, which is what the target's bytes say. Semantics are unchanged in both directions (both perform exactly the two volatile reads and no transfer). NEW CONSTRAINT discovered here and confirmed a second time on AddLocatorInstList in the same session -- see claim.law.IT_empty-bodied-if-elides-its-own-comparison.20260901.v1: an empty-bodied `if` is elided WHOLE by the MWCC front end, comparison and all, so it is NOT the lever for reproducing a dead compare; only volatile-qualified operand reads survive it.
attributes.law_screen: claim.law.EN-ops-multiset-cannot-classify-a-residual-run-slotdiff-first.20260901.v1 APPLIED, and its COROLLARY was decisive: slotdiff reported SLOT MAP IDENTICAL (frame 32/32, saves r27/r27) and regnorm reported 31 STRUCTURAL rows -- but every one of those rows is a branch whose target differs by exactly 12 bytes (T 0x228/O 0x21c, T 0x204/O 0x1f8, T 0x25c/O 0x250, ...), i.e. pure displacement from the 3-instruction deficit, exactly the artifact class the law names. Confirming the displacement arithmetic collapsed a 31-row 'structural' residual to ONE real cluster. claim.law.br-extern-ghost-and-volatile-scaffold-are-one-lever.20260901.v1 SCREENED and CONFIRMED from the cost side: the pre-existing volatile scaffold on the two s8 reads is load-bearing and correct (see residual for the two-extsb proof), so it was kept, not removed. claim.law.insn-count-parity-outranks-local-opcode-fidelity.20260831.v1 APPLIED as the arbiter between the two candidate forms. claim.law.SP_initializer-presence-outranks-declaration-position-in-callee-saved-numbering.20260901.v1 SCREENED for the named-temp form and explains its regression (the temps entered the initialized group and rotated the colouring). attributes.residual: STRUCTURAL, exactly 3 instructions and nothing else: target-only +1 cmpw +2 extsb at @c0-c8; ours-only is NONE, so every instruction we emit is correct and we are simply short a dead signed compare. The TWO extsb are the key evidence and they settle the semantics: MWCC would have CSE'd the already-sign-extended it1->data[6] from the immediately preceding live compare at @a0 (which needs only ONE extsb), so the target re-reads BOTH operands -- which is precisely what the volatile scaffold reproduces. The scaffold is therefore semantically right and must not be removed. What is missing is only the compare instruction itself, emitted by the original's expression phase and left behind when its branch was folded. HANDOFF: this is one dead compare with a fully understood mechanism and an empty ours-only set; it is a good harvest-lane / postprocessor candidate, or a target for whichever source form makes MWCC emit a comparison whose branch is later folded (the empty-body form is now measured NOT to be that form).
